blocks.text: Marketing systems that lower CAC, grow retention, and scale!

I help startups and scale-ups build the marketing engine they need to grow — connecting acquisition, CRM, retention, analytics, and creative execution into one practical system grounded in real customer data.
Head of CRM
Telegram // Linkedin // WhatsApp // Email // CMO.bio
Building retention into the #1 revenue channel for businesses.
What I Do the Best
I take CRM from "one of the channels" to the dominant revenue engine.
Across CMO-tenures and Head-of-CRM roles, I've built CRM functions from zero, scaled teams up to 18 people, and led transformations where CRM became the primary driver of growth.
What I'm strongest at:
– Building CRM functions from scratch in marketplace and consumer e-commerce contexts
– Designing customer data architectures and behavioral segmentation frameworks
– Leading teams across strategy, lifecycle, analytics, and execution
– Applying A/B testing at scale and decile analysis to find real audience and growth levers
– Bridging data, product, and brand stakeholders to align CRM with business outcomes
Selected Outcomes
A handful of moments that show how I work.
Yandex Eats → Foodtech / Marketplace

Built the CRM function from scratch at one of the two leaders of Russian food delivery. Within one quarter: +5% incremental revenue on a mature product, measured via control group. Team grew from 3 to 18-20 people. Designed a behavioral brand affinity matrix across tens of thousands of brands.
KupiVip → Online Fashion Discounter

Led marketing at one of Russia's largest fashion flash-sales marketplaces during a turnaround year. CRM share of revenue 11% → 74% in 11 months. Drove the first positive EBITDA in company history. Rebuilt audience strategy through decile analysis + deep interviews.
Out of Cloud (CRM Agency) → 30+ Enterprise Clients

Acted as Head of CRM across a portfolio including Vprok.ru (X5), Haier, JBL/Harman, Vita Pharmacies. Built the strategist function from 1 to 10 people in 16 months. Published client outcomes: Vprok CRM share 5% → 10% (+200M RUB), Haier capture rate 0.67% → 1.2%, JBL CPL 2.7x below benchmark.
Confidential E-commerce Marketplace (2025–present) → Fashion / Group-buy

Currently CMO at a regional marketplace with no paid acquisition channel by design. In 8 months: email revenue per delivered message 1.8 → 7 RUB (4x), channel revenue 5x, popup cart buyout rate 12% → 45%. Protected social channels through platform disruption (+1.8x). All with less than 1 FTE on CRM.
Svyaznoy → Mobile Tech Retail, 3,500 Stores

Loyalty function lead for one of the largest Russian retail chains of its era. Transactions per user 1.2 → 4.1. Designed the decile analysis methodology and "Methylene Blue Method" framework I now apply across every retail and digital project.

cards.desc: Built CRM and owned channels into the entire growth engine of a fashion-focused regional marketplace with no paid acquisition by design. In 8 months: quadrupled email revenue per delivered message, brought popup buyout from 12% to 45%, all with sub-1 FTE on CRM.
cards.body:
Regional fashion-discount marketplace with a group-buy model and no paid acquisition channel by design → CRM and owned channels are the entire growth engine

  • CRM channel reform (email + popup, stack: Mindbox). Email reputation low → good in 8 months. Revenue per delivered email 1.8 → 7 RUB (4x). Email channel revenue 1.5M RUB/month → 7.2M RUB/month (5x). Popup cart buyout rate 12% → 45% (3.75x), popup channel revenue 7M → 12M RUB/month.
  • Social channels resilience. Telegram and other social platforms drove ~20% of company revenue at start. Grew channel revenue 1.8x despite Russian platform bans and Telegram throttling → integrated MAX as a parallel platform, automated production workflow, restructured the team, introduced advanced analytics. Team of 4 regional specialists plus one strong lead.
  • Audience discovery → repositioning. Used decile analysis + deep interviews to identify the real core audience → women 40+ with discretionary income, buying for abundance ("get 3 dresses for the price of 1"), not for quality. Shifted communication tone, content curation, and frequency dynamics under this insight. Increased ARPU without deeper discounting.
  • Operating as player-manager across a small marketing org → owned strategy, hands-on execution and team development with no paid budget cover. Personally in Mindbox dashboards, segmentation logic, A/B test design.

    • Reflection. Marketing exceeded its targets, but bottleneck for company-level growth sat in product, not channels. Made the call to move on once my CRM expertise was no longer the highest-leverage thing I could bring. Senior is knowing when to step away as well as when to step in.

cards.desc: Led marketing during a turnaround year at one of Russia's largest fashion flash-sales marketplaces. Grew CRM share of revenue from 11% to 74% in 11 months, driving the first positive EBITDA in company history. Rebuilt audience strategy through decile analysis and deep interviews.
cards.body:
Aug 2014 – Jun 2015 → joined as CMO during a turnaround year. 48 direct reports across 5 functional sub-departments. 4 of 5 sub-leads vacant on day one. 18 KPIs handed down from the investor board.

  • CRM share of revenue 11% → 74% in 11 months. Built the rebuild around four parallel layers: in-house recommendation engine (72-page algorithm including behavioral data and look-a-like models), email frequency tied to daily site conversion, "preserves" library for external event triggers (weather, holidays, news), and base segmentation by behavioral response.
  • Counter-intuitive frequency move. Raised email frequency from 5 to 7 per day with no rise in unsubscribes — after data and interviews showed users perceived emails as service, not spam, because of the flash-sales business model. Communication frequency is a function of perceived value of the channel, not a universal best-practice.
  • Audience strategy reversal via decile analysis. Ran decile-revenue analysis + 10 deep interviews with the top decile → discovered the real core audience was 10–15 years older than the brand-book persona, 2 sizes larger, and motivated by quality (fabric, cut, finish), not aspiration. Reversed the brand strategy from aspirational-discount to quality-recognition. This rewrote tone of voice, product curation, creatives, and campaign calendar.
  • Marketing organization rebuild. Recruited senior CRM and brand leads from my network at Svyaznoy (during its takeover period) → saved 3–6 months of ramp-up. Built reporting automation (Access + Looker BI) personally to handle 18 quarterly KPIs without adding overhead to the team.
  • Outcomes. All 18 marketing KPIs delivered for the year. Reported the first positive EBITDA in the company's history at the second quarterly investor meeting. CRM became the dominant sales channel — not "one of," but the channel.

    • Reflection. Three lessons. First → CRM-best-practices are guidelines, not laws. Always test them against actual user behavior before applying. Second → simple methods first, ML later. The 2014 recommendation engine on 72 pages of behavioral logic worked because we didn't need ML for tactical recommendations. Third → discount marketplaces can reposition, but only if you find the real audience first. The KupiVip playbook doesn't translate directly to every discount-marketplace — each base has its own audience, its own motive. The methodology of finding that audience is what's transferable.

cards.desc: Led the loyalty function for one of the largest Russian retail chains of its era (3,500 stores, 18M loyalty members). Transactions per user grew from 1.2 to 4.1. Designed the decile analysis methodology and "Methylene Blue Method" framework I now apply in every retail and digital project.
cards.body:
CMO of Retail Loyalty Programs, Svyaznoy → Mobile Tech Retail (3,500 Stores)

Sep 2010 – Jun 2014 → led the loyalty function for one of the largest Russian retail chains of its era. 18M loyalty program participants, 7,200 connected retail points (Svyaznoy + coalition partners).

  • Transactions per user 1.2 → 4.1 across the full loyalty period. Built through coalition program rebuild (70+ partner brands across food, fashion, electronics, pharmacy, online), behavioral segmentation, and a redesigned cross-brand acquisition layer (2,000 unique mechanics over 18 months).
  • Decile analysis methodology design. Created the framework I now apply across every retail and digital project. Loyalty base ranked by 12-month rolling revenue, cut into deciles. Distribution recurs across industries: 0.3% of users generate 10% of revenue, first 2 deciles = 20% of revenue, last 6 deciles = 60% of users with minimal contribution.
  • "Methylene Blue Method" framework. Discovered that the first decile of customers behaves as a leading indicator for future mass-market hits. They buy in small volumes today what becomes mass-market in 1–2 years. Phone cases at Svyaznoy in 2012 are the canonical example — top decile bought them, fifth decile didn't; within a year, cases became the highest-margin accessory category. Strategy: find the "stained" products in top-decile baskets, move them to center shelf before mass demand catches up.
  • Assortment matrix reform pilot. Applied the decile playbook to assortment management. 15 experimental stores + 15 control stores. After one quarter → +5% incremental revenue on the experimental group. The reform concept became the new chain-wide standard and rollout reached a significant portion of the network before being interrupted by an ownership transition.

    • Reflection. Different deciles serve different business jobs. Last 1–2 deciles → cost control, served at minimal expense, sometimes blocked entirely. Middle deciles → growth, classic RFM logic. First decile → R&D indicator, not a revenue-growth target. This re-framing of decile analysis is what I now bring as the starting tool to every retail or digital CRM project.
